newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot natgas mostly lower ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot natgas mostly lower ahead of weekend.

text.p: U.S. spot natural gas prices were steady to lower Friday following a week-long rollercoaster ride in both the cash and futures markets.
At 1334 EDT, NYMEX's September contract was cents higher at $2.55, still cents below the contract high of $2.605 set earlier this week.
On the Louisiana Gulf Coast, prices at the Henry Hub eased by about four cents to the low-$2.50s but were still about 15 cents ahead of week-ago levels.
In the Midwest, where warmer weather has boosted cooling demand for the weekend, prices held in the low-to-mid $2.40s, remaining nearly 20 cents higher than week-ago levels.
At the Chicago city-gate, prices were also quoted from $2.55 early to the low-$2.60s shortly before nomination deadlines.
In the Permian Basin, where more supply was available, prices fell five cents to the $2.35-2.43, while Waha was pressured by two cents to the mid-to-high $2.40s.
El Paso's Keystone Mainline Station in Texas, where about 400 million cubic feet per day had been affected at receipt points in the Permian Basin since Tuesday, returned to service.
Southern California border prices similarly dropped six cents to $2.38-2.50.
In the East, prices at the New York city gate remained firm in the mid-$2.70s as temperature highs were forecast to reach 93 degrees F Sunday, according to Weather Services Corp.
